section_summary: This section covers State Department records from November 1942 to June 1943 concerning internal Japanese political administration, wartime constitutional adaptations, and major diplomatic realignments. It contains citizen correspondence forwarding a prophetic 1926 letter by Dr. Inazo Nitobe to propose anti-war propaganda highlighting pre-war Japanese liberalism; a detailed Division of Far Eastern Affairs study examining the centralization of colonial administration under the Ministry of Greater East Asiatic Affairs, the abolition of the Overseas Ministry, the 1942 'reformation' Diet elections, and the expansion of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association and Political Society; and extensive American, Chinese, and British diplomatic analyses of the April 1943 Tojo Cabinet reorganization, focusing on Foreign Minister Mamoru Shigemitsu's role in suspected Axis maneuvers to broker a separate Russo-German peace while executing a conciliatory policy toward Chinese puppet regimes.

subfiles.about: Brooklyn lawyer Harry Heller sends Joseph C. Grew an enclosed photostatic copy of a June 25, 1926 letter from Dr. Inazo Nitobe and proposes compiling statements of pre-war Japanese liberals to counter Japanese war propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Harry Heller sends Grew a 1926 Nitobe letter and suggests a pamphlet of peace statements by Japanese statesmen to counter the myth of indivisible fanaticism.
subfiles.title: Letter from Harry Heller to Joseph C. Grew Enclosing 1926 Letter from Dr. Inazo Nitobe

subfiles.about: Joseph C. Grew acknowledges Harry Heller's letter and refers it to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Grew, leaving on a speaking tour, refers Heller's letter and suggestion to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph C. Grew to Harry Heller

subfiles.about: Robert L. Smyth informs Harry Heller that his proposal to compile statements of Japanese statesmen has been referred to government propaganda agencies including the Office of War Information.
subfiles.summary: Smyth tells Heller his suggestion for publishing statements by Japanese statesmen is being brought to OWI and other agencies.
subfiles.title: Letter from Robert L. Smyth to Harry Heller

subfiles.about: A State Department research memorandum detailing wartime administrative reorganizations, colonial governance, and political consolidation in the Japanese Empire.
keywords: Ministry of Greater East Asiatic Affairs
subfiles.summary: This memorandum prepared by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs surveys major administrative trends in Japan since the outbreak of the Pacific War, focusing on centralized colonial control and increasing military direction under nominal civilian forms. It examines the April 1942 Diet election conducted under an 'officially recommended' candidate system directed by General Nobuyuki Abe's IRAA nominating council, the expansion and bureau reorganization of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, and the establishment of the Imperial Rule Assistance Political Society. The study further analyzes the abolition of the parliamentary vice-minister system, administrative personnel mobilization for southern occupied areas, the creation of the Ministry of Greater East Asiatic Affairs, the abolition of the Overseas Ministry, closer integration of Chosen, Taiwan, and Karafuto into home administration, and the severe curtailment of the Foreign Office's authority following Foreign Minister Togo's resignation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Administrative Changes in the Japanese Empire since the Outbreak of War

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum analyzing wartime Japanese administrative restructuring, colonial governance, and political centralization.
keywords: Ministry of Greater East Asiatic Affairs
subfiles.summary: This document is a duplicate carbon copy of the November 30, 1942 research memorandum prepared in the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. It provides an extensive overview of wartime administrative restructuring within Japan and its colonial empire, highlighting the April 1942 'reformation election' for the Diet, the evolving roles of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association and the Imperial Rule Assistance Political Society, and the training of administrative cadres for occupied southern territories. It also examines the creation of the Ministry of Greater East Asiatic Affairs, the dissolution of the Overseas Ministry, the extension of central cabinet ministries' jurisdictions over Chosen and Taiwan, the incorporation of Karafuto under the Home Ministry, and the downgrading of the Foreign Office under Masayuki Tani.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Administrative Changes in the Japanese Empire since the Outbreak of War (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Harry Heller thanks Robert L. Smyth for his communication and requests to be kept informed regarding his propaganda proposal.
subfiles.summary: Heller thanks Smyth for the Department's intended use of his Nitobe document and asks to be told of developments.
subfiles.title: Letter from Harry Heller to Robert L. Smyth

subfiles.about: Chungking Embassy reports views of Chinese Foreign Office Information Director Shao Yu-lin regarding Mamoru Shigemitsu's appointment as Foreign Minister and Axis efforts toward a Russo-German separate peace.
subfiles.summary: Vincent relays Chinese official Shao Yu-lin's view that Shigemitsu's appointment is part of an Axis effort to push Russia toward separate peace with Germany; Japan may attack Russia if it fails.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 587 from Chungking regarding Japanese Foreign Minister Appointment and Peace Moves

subfiles.about: Confidential paraphrase of Telegram No. 587 summarizing Chinese Foreign Office interpretations of Shigemitsu's appointment and Axis peace strategy toward Russia.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 587 for ONI and MID: Shigemitsu's appointment serves an Axis push for a Russo-German peace; Japan might attack the USSR if diplomacy fails.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 587 from Chungking regarding Appointment of Shigemitsu

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Hull communicates British and State Department appraisals of the Japanese Cabinet reorganization and Shigemitsu's appointment.
subfiles.summary: Hull relays British and State Department analysis of the Tojo cabinet reorganization: not a move to compromise peace but to streamline administration and consolidate control, with Shigemitsu suited for Soviet matters.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 561 to Chungking regarding Reorganization of Japanese Cabinet and Shigemitsu's Foreign Policy

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing an Ankara telegram reporting a conversation with returning Turkish Ambassador to Japan Ferid Tek on conditions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Ankara Telegram No. 826 (May 18, 1943): Steinhardt's conversation with Turkish Ambassador Ferit Tek on wartime Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet regarding Conditions in Japan from Ferid Tek

subfiles.about: Internal State Department routing memorandum recommending the enclosures of Chungking Despatch No. 1128 analyzing the Tojo Cabinet reorganization.
subfiles.summary: Routing memo draws attention to Chungking Despatch No. 1128: Shao Yu-lin's analysis of Japanese cabinet changes and Wang Peng-sheng's speculation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Chungking Despatch No. 1128 concerning Japanese Cabinet Changes

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a memorandum of conversation with Shao Yu-lin and an editorial from the Ta Kung Pao analyzing the Tojo Cabinet reorganization.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires a.i. John Carter Vincent transmits Chinese analyses of the April 20, 1943 partial reorganization of the Tojo Cabinet. Enclosure 1 is Carl H. Boehringer's memorandum of an April 23 interview with Chinese Information Director Shao Yu-lin, who argues that Foreign Minister Mamoru Shigemitsu was appointed to mediate a Russo-German separate peace and achieve Soviet rapprochement, or to justify an eventual anti-Soviet attack as a crusade against Bolshevism. Enclosure 2 is an English translation of an April 23 editorial from the Ta Kung Pao (inspired by General Wang Peng-sheng) asserting that Tojo's cabinet reshuffle reflects growing weakness, that the reorganization followed Hitler's directives via German Ambassador Stahmer, and that appointments of Shigemitsu, Ando, Amau, Yamazaki, and Oasa signal aggressive Axis coordination and intensified exploitation of occupied China.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1128: Interpretations of Recent Japanese Cabinet Changes (with Enclosures)

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Despatch No. 1128 and its enclosures analyzing the domestic and international implications of the Tojo Cabinet reshuffle.
subfiles.summary: This subfile is a duplicate copy of Chungking Despatch No. 1128, including the covering despatch by John Carter Vincent, Carl H. Boehringer's memorandum of conversation with Shao Yu-lin (Enclosure 1), and the translated Ta Kung Pao editorial inspired by General Wang Peng-sheng (Enclosure 2, which continues past page 121). The documents assess the strategic significance of the Tojo Cabinet reorganization, comparing Shao Yu-lin's view that Japan was pursuing pragmatic diplomatic mediation with Russia against General Wang's view that Tokyo was operating under direct German direction and planning new aggressive outrages abroad.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1128: Interpretations of Recent Japanese Cabinet Changes (Duplicate Copy with Enclosures)
